items.title: Added terminalSequence field to hook JSON output so hooks can emit desktop notifications, window titles, and bells without a controlling terminal

explanation.what_it_is: The terminalSequence field is a new addition to hook JSON output, allowing hooks to generate specific terminal sequences, such as desktop notifications, window titles, and bells, even when not connected to a controlling terminal.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to create more interactive and attention-grabbing hooks, even in headless or automated environments, by providing a way to emit visual and auditory cues.
how_to_use: Use the terminalSequence field to trigger desktop notifications when a hook completes or encounters an error
Set the terminalSequence field to change the window title of the terminal running the hook
Emit a bell sound using the terminalSequence field to draw attention to a completed hook

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS to clone GitHub plugin sources over HTTPS instead of SSH, for environments without a GitHub SSH key

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS setting allows cloning GitHub plugin sources over HTTPS instead of SSH.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting is useful for environments that don't have a GitHub SSH key, enabling them to clone plugins without additional setup.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS to true in your environment variables to clone GitHub plugins over HTTPS.

items.title: Added ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID environment variable for workload identity federation — scopes the minted token to a specific workspace when the…

explanation.what_it_is: The ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID environment variable allows scoping of minted tokens to a specific workspace for workload identity federation.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more fine-grained control over access and authentication within Claude Code, particularly in multi-workspace environments.
how_to_use: Set the ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID environment variable to the ID of the workspace you want to scope the minted token to.
Use this variable in conjunction with workload identity federation to manage access to specific workspaces.

items.title: Added claude agents --cwd <path> to scope the session list to a directory

explanation.what_it_is: The claude agents command now accepts a --cwd option, which allows you to specify a directory to scope the session list to.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables Claude Code users to filter the session list by a specific directory, making it easier to manage sessions for projects with multiple directories.
how_to_use: Run `claude agents --cwd /path/to/project` to list sessions only for the specified project directory
Use `--cwd` to narrow down the session list when working with multiple projects in different directories

items.title: Fast mode (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 4.7
items.summary: Fast mode (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 4.7. Set speed: "fast" with model: "claude-opus-4-7" and the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header for significantly faster output token generation at…

explanation.what_it_is: Fast mode is a research preview feature that generates output tokens significantly faster than standard mode, now compatible with Claude Opus 4.7 model.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to leverage the faster output token generation of fast mode with the capabilities of the Claude Opus 4.7 model, potentially accelerating development and testing workflows.
how_to_use: Set speed: 'fast' with model: 'claude-opus-4-7' to enable fast mode
Include the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header in your API requests

items.title: Added agent view (Research Preview): a single list of every Claude Code session — running, blocked on you, or done. Run claude agents to get started.…

explanation.what_it_is: The agent view is a single list that displays all Claude Code sessions, including running, blocked, and completed sessions. This view is currently in Research Preview.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows Claude Code users to easily track and manage all their sessions from one place, simplifying workflow and reducing the need to switch between multiple views.
how_to_use: Run the command 'claude agents' to access the agent view
Use the agent view to monitor running sessions and identify blocked sessions that require user input

items.title: Added /goal command: set a completion condition and Claude keeps working across turns until it's met. Works in interactive, -p, and Remote Control.…

explanation.what_it_is: The /goal command allows you to set a completion condition for Claude to work towards, enabling it to continue working across multiple turns until the condition is met.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to create more complex and open-ended tasks that require multiple interactions to complete, streamlining their workflow and reducing the need for manual intervention.
how_to_use: Use /goal to set a specific completion condition, such as 'generate 5 code snippets' or 'reach a certain accuracy threshold'
Combine /goal with interactive or -p modes to work on tasks that require multiple iterations
Utilize /goal in Remote Control to automate tasks that need to run across multiple turns without manual intervention

items.title: Added /scroll-speed command to tune mouse wheel scroll speed with a live preview

explanation.what_it_is: The /scroll-speed command allows users to adjust the speed of their mouse wheel scroll in Claude Code, with a live preview to see the changes in real-time.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives users more control over their workflow, enabling them to customize the scroll speed to their preference, which can be particularly useful for tasks that require precise scrolling.
how_to_use: Use the /scroll-speed command to adjust the scroll speed, and observe the live preview to find the optimal setting for your needs.
Experiment with different scroll speeds to find the one that works best for your specific tasks, such as scrolling through long code files or navigating complex interfaces.

items.title: Added claude plugin details <name> to show a plugin's component inventory and projected per-session token cost

explanation.what_it_is: The `claude plugin details <name>` command displays a plugin's component inventory and estimated per-session token cost.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to better understand the composition and potential costs of their plugins, enabling more informed decisions about plugin usage.
how_to_use: Run `claude plugin details my_plugin` to view the component inventory and projected token cost for a specific plugin.
Use this command to compare the costs of different plugins and optimize token usage.

items.title: Added transcript view navigation: ? for keyboard shortcuts, {/} to jump between user prompts, v to toggle shortcut panel

explanation.what_it_is: Transcript view navigation allows users to move through transcripts using keyboard shortcuts, including ? for shortcut lists, {/} to jump between user prompts, and v to toggle the shortcut panel.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update streamlines the process of reviewing and navigating transcripts, making it easier for users to work with large conversations.
how_to_use: Press ? to view available keyboard shortcuts
Use {/} to quickly jump between user prompts in a transcript
Toggle the shortcut panel with v to customize your workflow

items.title: Added hook args: string[] field (exec form) that spawns the command directly without a shell, so path placeholders never need quoting

explanation.what_it_is: A new hook args field that allows spawning commands directly without a shell, using an array of strings as arguments.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change eliminates the need to quote path placeholders, simplifying command execution and reducing potential errors.
how_to_use: Pass command arguments as an array of strings to avoid shell interpretation
Use this feature to execute commands with file paths containing special characters without quoting

items.title: Added hook continueOnBlock config option for PostToolUse — set to true to feed the hook's rejection reason back to Claude and continue the turn

explanation.what_it_is: The continueOnBlock config option for PostToolUse hooks allows you to feed the hook's rejection reason back to Claude and continue the turn when set to true.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to handle hook rejections more gracefully, allowing the conversation to continue even when a hook is blocked.
how_to_use: Set continueOnBlock to true in your PostToolUse hook config to enable this behavior
Use this option to provide a better user experience by handling hook rejections and continuing the conversation

items.title: We've launched Claude Platform on AWS, bringing the Claude API to…
items.summary: We've launched Claude Platform on AWS, bringing the Claude API to Anthropic-managed infrastructure accessible through AWS, with AWS billing and IAM authentication. Access the full Messages API, Files…

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude Platform is now available on AWS, allowing access to the Claude API through Anthropic-managed infrastructure with AWS billing and IAM authentication.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows Claude Code users to leverage AWS's infrastructure and authentication capabilities, streamlining their workflow and potentially reducing costs.
how_to_use: Access the full Messages API through AWS
Use AWS IAM authentication to manage access to the Claude API
Utilize AWS billing for Claude API usage

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL to re-enable the session quality survey for enterprises capturing responses through OpenTelemetry

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL setting allows enterprises to re-enable the session quality survey for users, specifically when responses are captured through OpenTelemetry.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it gives enterprises the option to collect user feedback on session quality again, which can inform improvements to their Claude Code implementation.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL to true in your environment variables to re-enable the session quality survey.
Use OpenTelemetry to capture user responses to the survey and integrate them into your enterprise's feedback loop.

items.title: Added settings.autoMode.hard_deny for auto mode classifier rules that block unconditionally regardless of user intent or allow exceptions

explanation.what_it_is: The settings.autoMode.hard_deny setting allows auto mode classifier rules to block unconditionally, ignoring user intent or allow exceptions. This setting provides a way to enforce strict rules in auto mode.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over auto mode classifier rules, enabling them to enforce strict rules without exceptions. This can be particularly useful for sensitive or high-stakes applications where flexibility is not desired.
how_to_use: Set settings.autoMode.hard_deny to true to enable unconditional blocking for specific classifier rules
Use this setting to enforce strict rules for certain topics or keywords, such as profanity or sensitive information

items.title: Added worktree.baseRef setting (fresh | head) to choose whether --worktree, EnterWorktree, and agent-isolation worktrees branch from origin/<default>…

explanation.what_it_is: The worktree.baseRef setting allows you to choose whether new worktrees branch from the origin's default branch or the current head, with options 'fresh' or 'head'.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives Claude Code users more control over their workflow, allowing them to decide whether new worktrees should start from a stable default branch or the latest changes in the repository.
how_to_use: Set worktree.baseRef to 'fresh' to create worktrees that branch from the origin's default branch
Set worktree.baseRef to 'head' to create worktrees that branch from the current head

items.title: Added sandbox.bwrapPath and sandbox.socatPath managed settings (Linux/WSL) to specify custom bubblewrap and socat binary locations

explanation.what_it_is: Two new managed settings, sandbox.bwrapPath and sandbox.socatPath, allow you to specify custom locations for bubblewrap and socat binaries on Linux and WSL systems.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives you more control over the dependencies used by Claude Code's sandboxing feature, which can be useful for custom or restricted environments.
how_to_use: Set sandbox.bwrapPath to a custom bubblewrap binary location, e.g. /usr/local/bin/bwrap
Set sandbox.socatPath to a custom socat binary location, e.g. /usr/local/bin/socat

items.title: Added parentSettingsBehavior admin-tier key ('first-wins' | 'merge') to let admins opt SDK managedSettings (parent tier) into the policy merge

explanation.what_it_is: The parentSettingsBehavior admin-tier key allows admins to control how SDK managed settings from the parent tier are merged into the policy, with options 'first-wins' or 'merge'.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives admins more flexibility in managing settings inheritance, enabling them to choose whether parent settings override or merge with child settings.
how_to_use: Set parentSettingsBehavior to 'first-wins' to prioritize parent settings over child settings
Set parentSettingsBehavior to 'merge' to combine parent and child settings

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable to the Bash tool subprocess environment, matching the session_id passed to hooks

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable is now available in the Bash tool subprocess environment, containing the same session ID passed to hooks.
explanation.why_it_matters: This allows scripts running in the Bash tool subprocess to access and utilize the current session ID, enabling more informed and session-aware automation.
how_to_use: Access the session ID in a Bash script using $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
Use the session ID to customize script behavior or logging

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1 env var to opt out of the fullscreen alternate-screen renderer and keep the conversation in the…

explanation.what_it_is: A new environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN that allows opting out of the fullscreen alternate-screen renderer.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows Claude Code users to keep conversations in the main terminal window instead of switching to a fullscreen alternate screen.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1 in your environment variables to disable the fullscreen renderer.
Run your Claude Code application with the environment variable set to keep conversations in the main terminal window.

items.title: Added a "Pasting…" footer hint while a Ctrl+V image paste is being read from the clipboard

explanation.what_it_is: A 'Pasting…' footer hint is now displayed when using Ctrl+V to paste an image from the clipboard, indicating that the paste operation is in progress.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update provides visual feedback to the user, reducing uncertainty about whether the paste operation has been registered by the application.
how_to_use: Use Ctrl+V to paste an image from the clipboard and observe the 'Pasting…' footer hint.
Wait for the hint to disappear, indicating that the image has been successfully pasted.

items.title: Added --plugin-url <url> flag to fetch a plugin .zip archive from a URL for the current session

explanation.what_it_is: The --plugin-url flag allows you to fetch a plugin .zip archive from a specified URL for the current Claude Code session.
explanation.why_it_matters: This flag enables users to load plugins from external sources without having to manually download and install them, streamlining the plugin installation process.
how_to_use: Run Claude Code with the --plugin-url flag followed by the URL of the plugin .zip archive, e.g. --plugin-url https://example.com/plugin.zip
Use this flag to load plugins from GitHub releases or other external repositories

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT=1 env var to force-enable synchronized output on terminals that auto-detection misses (e.g. Emacs eat)

explanation.what_it_is: A new environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT that allows you to force-enable synchronized output in terminals where auto-detection fails.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it ensures that Claude Code's output is properly synchronized in terminals like Emacs, where auto-detection may not work correctly.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT=1 in your environment variables to enable synchronized output in terminals that are not auto-detected.
Use this variable in Emacs or other terminals where Claude Code's output was previously not synchronized.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE: when set on Homebrew or WinGet installations, Claude Code runs the upgrade command in the background…

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE setting allows Claude Code to automatically run the upgrade command in the background for installations managed by Homebrew or WinGet.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting streamlines the upgrade process for users who install or manage Claude Code via package managers, reducing the need for manual updates.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE on your Homebrew installation to enable automatic background updates.
Set CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE on your WinGet installation to enable automatic background updates.

explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows Claude Code users to access and test these features, providing earlier access to upcoming functionality.

Test and provide feedback on these features to shape their development.
